evidence: Filled Add Entry form (Task Name, Priority, Due Date, Completed, Score) and submitted; new row "Automated Test Entry 5 Dec 25, 2026 42" appeared immediately in table, entry count went from 5 to 6.

Configure Fields dialog shows existing fields of type Text (Task Name), Number (Priority), Date (Due Date), Checkbox (Completed). Created a new field "Score" of type Number via the "New field name" input + type combobox (options: Text, Number, Date, Checkbox) + Add button; new column appeared in table immediately.

Entered text "Automated Test Entry", number 5, date 2026-12-25, checkbox toggled to Yes, and number 42 for Score field; all values saved and displayed correctly in the new row (text, "5", "Dec 25, 2026", check icon, "42").

DOM check: checked entries render a green check icon (class "lucide-check text-success"), unchecked entries render a gray X icon (class "lucide-x text-muted-foreground") - clearly visually distinguishable.

Clicked "Cards" button: view switched to a card grid layout showing each entry as a card with field label/value pairs. Clicked "Table" button: view switched back to tabular layout with columns. Both transitions were immediate with no reload.

Sort menu lists all fields (Task Name, Priority, Due Date, Completed, Score). Selecting "Priority" sorted entries ascending (1,1,2,2,3,5); clicking again toggled to descending (5,3,2,2,1,1). Footer status text updated to "Sorted by Priority (ascending/descending)".
Clicking a sort field in the Sort menu immediately re-ordered the entries and updated the footer label ("Sorted by Priority (ascending)") without any page reload or delay.

Compared all 6 entries' field values before and after sorting ascending/descending by Priority: Task Name, Due Date, Completed and Score values for every entry remained identical, only row order changed, confirming no data was altered or lost.

actual: No filter UI exists anywhere in the app. Searched the full header/toolbar (Fields, Search box, Sort, Table/Cards toggle, Add Entry) and DOM (no elements with 'filter' in class/id/aria-label/title/data-testid), and right-clicked column headers - no filter control or criteria-based filtering mechanism was found. Only a free-text search box exists, which does not let users filter by specific field criteria (e.g., checkbox status, numeric/date range).

Since no filter functionality is implemented in the application (see FT-6), it is impossible to verify that filters accurately include/exclude entries without data loss - the feature does not exist to test.

evidence: In table view, used the drag-handle's keyboard-accessible sortable control (Space to pick up, ArrowDown to move, Space to drop) to move "Design new landing page" down one position. Status announced "Draggable item entry-1 was dropped over droppable area entry-2" and the resulting row order (Review, Design, Update, Prepare, Team, Automated) exactly matched the manual operation performed. Order persisted after switching away and back to Table view.

Priority/Score fields are rendered as native <input type="number"> spinbuttons. Attempting to type non-numeric text "abc" into the Priority field was rejected outright ("Cannot type text into input[type=number]"), confirming only numeric input is accepted.

Due Date field is a native <input type="date">. Attempting to type "invalid-date" was rejected ("Malformed value"). Directly setting the value to an invalid date "2026-13-45" (month 13, day 45) resulted in the input value being cleared to empty string, confirming invalid dates are rejected.

issue: Missing required-field validation on Add Entry
actual: Opened "Add New Entry" dialog, left the Task Name field completely blank (undefined), and clicked "Add Entry". The entry was still added successfully (entry count went from 6 to 7) with an empty Task Name cell (verified via DOM: cell text was ""), Priority "0", Score "0". The app does not prevent adding an entry when a field's value is left undefined/blank, contradicting the requirement that "an entry cannot be added" if at least one field is not defined.

Clicked the delete (trash) icon button on a table row. The entry was removed immediately (entry count dropped from 7 to 6) with no confirmation dialog, prompt, or undo option appearing at any point - contradicting the requirement that a confirmation button/dialog should appear before deletion to prevent accidental deletes.

evidence: Typing "Review" into the search box immediately filtered the table to 1 matching entry ("Review marketing materials") and updated footer to "1 entry matching \"Review\"". Clearing the search restored all 6 entries instantly.

Compared all 6 entries between Table view (columns: Task Name, Priority, Due Date, Completed, Score) and Card view (labeled field rows per card). Values matched exactly in both views, e.g. "Automated Test Entry" showed Priority 5, Due Date Dec 25 2026, Completed Yes, Score 42 identically in both layouts. No entries or field values were missing or truncated in either view.

In Table view, each column header clearly displays the field label (Task Name, Priority, Due Date, Completed, Score) and the Configure Fields dialog explicitly labels each field's type (Text/Number/Date/Checkbox) next to its name. In Card view, each field is shown as a labeled row ("Priority", "Due Date", "Completed", "Score") paired with a type-appropriate icon and formatted value (e.g. calendar icon for dates, check/x icon for checkbox), making labels and types clearly distinguishable in both view modes.
